extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers, economists, and policymakers studying patents, startups, and entrepreneurial finance (VC and patent-collateral lending)
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical research task that measures how patent application outcomes (first-action approval/rejection) causally affect startup outcomes (employment, sales, VC funding, collateralized lending, follow-on innovation) using instrumental-variables and panel methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO patentability requirements (novelty, non-obviousness, utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are certified to have cleared the USPTO’s requirements of novelty, non-obviousness, and utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper treats an issued patent as a quality/market-power signal because it has satisfied these statutory requirements; this underlies hypotheses that patent grants affect investor behavior and startup outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateralizability of patents and patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Firms frequently pledge their patent rights as collateral; firms can pledge pending patent applications (after first-action but before final approval) and even rejected patent applications as part of a bundle of intangible assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejected applications may still serve as prior art and a description of the holder’s intellectual assets, but approval increases likelihood of securing a collateralized patent loan (e.g., first-application approval raises probability of pledging that application as collateral by 8.6 percentage points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examiner approval rate as an instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: The past approval rate of the patent examiner reviewing an application is used as an instrument (IV) for whether the application is approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification assumes quasi-random assignment of applications to examiners within art-unit-by-application-year. The first-stage must be strong and robust to potential assignment threats; the paper includes art-unit-by-year fixed effects and tests for quality-based or examiner-characteristic-based assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear-probability model with art-unit-by-application-year fixed effects (instead of duration models)
rubrics_metrics.description: To handle right-censoring while accommodating instrumental-variable techniques, the paper estimates a simple linear-probability model with art-unit-by-application-year fixed effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration models are the traditional way to handle right-censoring but cannot easily be combined with IV in this context, motivating the linear-probability choice; fixed effects control for differential time available to go public across application years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm survival (variable definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm survival during year t after the first-action decision on a firm’s first patent application is set to 1 if the firm is matched with the NETS sample and employment (or sales) data are available either for the year t or for any year after t; set to zero otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This coding treats absence of NETS match or data as non-survival; implies conservative handling of missing downstream data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment growth (post-first-action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment growth after the first-action decision on a firm’s first (or second) patent application is employment_{t+k} / employment_{t-1}, where t is the first-action year and k = 1…5. If a firm dies and does not appear in NETS in year t+k, employment_{t+k} = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horizon analyses are reported for k = 1 through 5 years; death is operationalized by setting future employment to zero, which affects measured growth rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales growth (post-first-action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales growth after the first-action decision on a firm’s first (or second) patent application is sales_{t+k} / sales_{t-1}, where t is the first-action year and k = 1…5. If a firm dies and does not appear in NETS in year t+k, sales_{t+k} = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to employment growth; measures reported over 1–5 year horizons and treat death as zero sales thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-patent-filing employment growth (baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-patent-filing employment growth is employment_{t} / employment_{t-1} − 1, where t is the year that a firm’s first patent application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a control or descriptive baseline for firms at time of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-patent-filing sales growth (baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-patent-filing sales growth is sales_{t} / sales_{t-1} − 1, where t is the year that a firm’s first patent application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used similarly as a baseline control or descriptive statistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of subsequent patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: No. subsequent patent applications is the number of applications with a filing date greater than the first-action date of a firm’s first (or second) application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts subsequent patenting activity to measure follow-on innovation intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of subsequent approved patents
rubrics_metrics.description: No. subsequent approved patents is the number of approved applications with a filing date greater than the first-action date of a firm’s first (or second) application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to separate quantity of filing from realized patent grants in follow-on innovation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval rate of subsequent patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval rate of subsequent patent applications is defined as (no. subsequent approved patents) / (no. subsequent patent applications). It is only defined for firms with at least one subsequent patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures average success of follow-on applications; sample restriction noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total citations to subsequent patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Total citations to all subsequent patent applications is the number of citations received by all subsequent patent applications combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This number is measured over the five years following each application’s public disclosure date (typically 18 months after filing); set to zero for firms with no subsequent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average citations-per-patent to subsequent approved patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Average citations-per-patent to subsequent approved patents is the average number of citations received by those subsequent patent applications that are approved. It is only defined for firms with at least one subsequent approved patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess the quality/impact of follow-on granted patents; defined only when denominator exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner experience (variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner experience is the number of years since the examiner joined the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a control/proxy in first-stage specifications to test for examiner-characteristic-based assignment and potential biases in instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner grade and signatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner grade is the examiner’s grade according to the government’s General Schedule (GS). Most examiners start at grade GS-7 or GS-9. Examiners at GS-7 through GS-11 need senior examiners to sign off on their decisions. GS-13 examiners undergo a period when they have partial signatory authority. Examiners at GS-14 and above have full signatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner grade is included as a covariate or robustness control because grade/seniority may correlate with approval behavior; column 6 of first-stage includes examiner experience and seniority proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experienced founder indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced founder is an indicator set equal to one if at least one of the up to five key executives of the startup listed in Standard & Poor’s Capital IQ database previously founded a different firm, according to the professional background provided by Capital IQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to proxy for prior entrepreneurial experience; the paper examines heterogeneous approval effects by founder experience (finding stronger effects for inexperienced founders).

rubrics_metrics.name: High startup agglomeration state indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: High startup agglomeration state is an indicator set equal to one if the startup is headquartered in a state with above median startup agglomeration in the year of the startup’s first patent application. Startup agglomeration is measured using the number of first-time patent applicants in the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test geographic heterogeneity: patent approval effects on VC funding are larger in high-agglomeration (hub) states like CA, MA, NY.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry classification by USPTO technology centers
rubrics_metrics.description: IT startups are those whose first patent application is reviewed by an examiner in tech centers 21, 24, 26, or 28. Biochemistry startups are those reviewed by tech centers 16 or 17. Other industries correspond to tech centers 36 or 37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry coding via art-unit/technology center is used to study heterogeneity: patent approval effects are significant for IT but not for biochemistry, reflecting differences in information value of patents across industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art-unit-by-application-year fixed effects to control timing/censoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Include art-unit-by-application-year fixed effects to control for the fact that startups that applied for their first patent in later years have had less time to go public (and to address quasi-random examiner assignment within art unit and year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed effects are central to identification strategy and to handling right-censoring in analyses of IPO/exit and follow-up outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneous-effect checks (dimensions to evaluate patent value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether financiers respond differently to patent grants across dimensions: number of prior VC rounds, prior founder experience, state startup agglomeration, industry, and subsequent patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subgroup analyses are presented to shed light on mechanisms (e.g., signaling vs monopoly value) and are explicitly described as suggestive rather than definitive; results show larger effects for early VC rounds, inexperienced founders, hubs, and IT industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2SLS first-stage specification and robustness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: First-stage regressions predict first patent-application approval using the examiner approval rate instrument; baseline includes art-unit-by-year fixed effects. Robustness checks control for applicant/application characteristics and examiner characteristics, and use technology-subclass-by-year fixed effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate by least squares; report heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors clustered at the art unit level and significance indicators (***, **, *). Varying the specification tests threats to quasi-random assignment of examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability caveat for NETS-matched outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment and sales data are only available for startups that can be matched to the National Establishment Time Series (NETS) database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample sizes and summary statistics for employment/sales-based outcomes are conditional on successful NETS matching; analyses acknowledge varying availability of observations and singletons.
